tagline: Along the top of Lake Michigan, bluff and beach by turns.
intro: From St. Ignace, US 2 heads west along the north shore of Lake Michigan, winding along tall bluffs and diving down to skirt miles of empty beach, through Brevort, Epoufette and Naubinway. Past Naubinway it runs south of Engadine, swings inland by Gould City and Blaney Park, then comes back to the lake for the last run into Manistique, 92 miles from where it began.
The lakeshore road out of St. Ignace was begun in 1936. Before that the highway went inland from Brevort. Long before either, the Sault and Green Bay Trail kept roughly to this same shore.

moments.title: Cut River Bridge
moments.text: The road crosses 147 feet above the gorge on a steel cantilever finished after the war, with stairs down into the valley and, under the east end, a door plaque reading "T. Troll".

moments.title: Naubinway
moments.text: The northernmost point of Lake Michigan is here, and in 1805 it was used to draw the western boundary of the new Michigan Territory.

moments.title: Manistique
moments.text: Named for its river, which was then spelled Monistique, the city owes its present spelling to a mistake in its charter.
